messages:
jamie: quick heads-up — the Python quickstart has two copy/paste issues causing onboarding friction
kevin: what happened?
jamie: the code sample uses REDWOOD_API_KEY but our SDK reads REDWOOD_API_TOKEN. new users are getting 401s and opening support tickets
sarah: where is that file?
jamie: docs/quickstarts/python/cheatsheet.md, top code block. also the example sets base_url = 'https://api.redwood.local' which is an internal hostname
kevin: ahhh that explains the DNS failures i saw in Sentry from trial orgs
jamie: exact snippet (buggy):
```python
import os
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(base_url="https://api.redwood.local", api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
```
sarah: recommended fix is to use our env var name and not inline tokens. update to: 
```python
import os
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(base_url="https://api.redwood.com", api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_TOKEN"))
```
kevin: can we also show the curl example as env-var only? ppl paste tokens into public gists
maria: yes please — add a short note: "never paste real tokens in public examples" and show `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_TOKEN\"`
jamie: i opened a minimal PR to fix the names + host + add the security note. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1023
docs-bot: PR 1023 merged into main by maria — includes test to catch non-production base_url values in code blocks
kevin: awesome. can we add a CI lint rule to fail if codeblocks contain "redwood.local" or literal-looking secrets?
sarah: i sketched a quick grep job: `grep -R "redwood.local\|REDWOOD_API_KEY" docs || exit 1` but better to integrate a docs-linter check
maria: adding to infra backlog. for now i patched the quickstart and bumped the docs version in the changelog
jamie: thanks all — i'll reply to the support thread we saw and close the loop with the user
kevin: small followup: should we standardize on REDWOOD_API_TOKEN vs REDWOOD_KEY? we have both in different repos
sarah: vote for REDWOOD_API_TOKEN and update SDK env parsing to support the legacy names with a deprecation warning
maria: agreed. i'll open a separate RFC for deprecations
jamie: perfect. that should reduce future copy/paste pain :thumbsup:
